why:
phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — `Context::config(&self, node_name) -> ExecutorConfig` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:126`): the one method on our `Context`, turning the resolved identity into the config `Executor::open` takes, with the node name supplied at the call because one process can open several nodes on one identity. rclrs has no counterpart: its `Context` is passed to `create_node` / `create_executor` directly, because it owns the rcl context those consume. Ours owns nothing (see `rust:Context`), so the seam between identity and session is an explicit conversion. Borrowing (`ExecutorConfig<'a>` over `&'a self`) is what keeps the config heap-free.

phase-467 Row 11 (2026-10-03) -- REFUSES a context that carries `--ros-args` remaps. An `ExecutorConfig` has nowhere to put them, so the executor `Executor::open` builds from it would never see them -- the silent drop `init_with_args` exists to prevent. It panics naming `create_executor` / `create_executor_in`, which install them. A context without remaps -- every context not built from an argv that carried `-r` -- is unaffected (`config_is_unaffected_without_remaps`).
